status: frozen before executing the active-pressure kinetic audit and without opening observational targets
purpose: Test the v17K/v17L derivative-disformal susceptibility on an explicit dynamical matter action. Derive the exact transverse principal coefficient after constraints, locate every positive-density zero surface, and retire the coupling if any allowed canonical-matter background makes the spin-1 sector singular or unstable.

authorization.allowed_outcome: retain or retire only the acceleration-dependent susceptibility in the physical metric

local_background.geometry: At one event use a locally inertial frame g_mn=eta_mn, U^m=(1,0,0,0), A_m=0, constant X with q_0=alpha X, and a homogeneous canonical scalar phi=y t with locally constant V.
local_background.justification: The high-frequency transverse principal symbol is local. Rotational symmetry prevents the transverse spin-1 mode from mixing with the scalar matter perturbation; the metric shift is removed by the standard Einstein-aether constraint reduction.
local_background.allowed_domain: 0<q_0<1/2, rho_hat>0, and 0<=p_hat<=rho_hat. These backgrounds have a Lorentzian physical metric and canonical matter satisfying the null and dominant energy conditions.
local_background.positive_branch: For positive pressure, the static stable-scalar Green function gives q=alpha X proportional to alpha^2 times the source, so the sourced branch connected to q=0 has q>=0 independently of the sign chosen for alpha.

explicit_matter_action.action_class: Canonical test matter completing the TeVeS-like derivative-disformal physical metric carried by the published Einstein-aether sector
explicit_matter_action.action: S_phi=-integral sqrt(-g_tilde)[g_tilde^mn partial_m phi partial_n phi/2+V]
explicit_matter_action.physical_metric: g_tilde_mn=exp(2q)[g_mn+2q U_m U_n], q=q_0 chi(Z), chi(Z)=(1+Z)^(-1/4), Z=c^4 A_m A^m/a_sigma^2
explicit_matter_action.rest_frame_metric: d s_tilde^2=exp(2q)[-(1-2q)dt^2+d x^2], so the matter light speed squared in g coordinates is 1-2q
explicit_matter_action.zero_q_fluid_map: rho=y^2/2+V and p=y^2/2-V, equivalently y^2=rho+p and V=(rho-p)/2
explicit_matter_action.small_q_identity: J(q)=3p+q(2rho+9p)+O(q^2), so rest energy re-enters the reciprocal source away from q=0 even when p is small.

dimensionless_normalization.definitions: rho_hat=8 pi G rho/a_sigma^2, p_hat=8 pi G p/a_sigma^2, J_hat=8 pi G J/a_sigma^2, and v_i=c^2 A_i/a_sigma

constrained_transverse_sector.matter_hessian: partial^2 L_phi_hat/partial v_i partial v_j at v=0=-(q_0 J_hat(q_0)/2) delta_ij
constrained_transverse_sector.spin_1_speed: s_1^2=epsilon/c_14,eff because c_13=0, c_1=epsilon, and c_3=-epsilon
constrained_transverse_sector.no_mixing_statement: At A=0, partial q/partial dot U_i=0, so the transverse U_i--phi velocity Hessian vanishes. A negative c_14,eff is therefore a negative principal direction of the exact dynamical system, not an artifact of freezing the stress tensor.
constrained_transverse_sector.zero_surface: For p_hat=w rho_hat, define F(q,w)=J_hat(q,rho_hat,w rho_hat)/rho_hat. The singular surface is rho_hat_crit=2 epsilon/[q F(q,w)] whenever F>0.

decision_rule: Retain the derivative susceptibility only if the exact matter Hessian matches finite differences, the scalar matter kinetic term is positive, c_14,eff and s_1^2 remain finite and positive on every allowed background, and no finite positive-density zero surface exists.

If c_14,eff reaches zero or becomes negative for any canonical matter background with 0<q<1/2 and 0<=p<=rho, retire chi(A^2) from the physical metric. Do not rescue it by refitting epsilon, because every finite epsilon merely moves a finite zero surface and epsilon is already frozen by the prior gravitational gate.

A failure retires the derivative matter coupling, not the published luminal Einstein-aether carrier and not the broader goal of deriving apparent halo scales from baryons. The next mechanism must avoid putting a term linear in A^2 inside the matter metric.

formula_inventory.equations: L_phi(q)=y^2 exp(2q)/[2 sqrt(1-2q)]-V exp(4q)sqrt(1-2q); J(0)=3p; J(q)=3p+q(2rho+9p)+O(q^2); c_14,eff=epsilon-q J_hat(q)/2; s_1^2=epsilon/c_14,eff; rho_hat_crit=2epsilon/[qF(q,w)]
